meta.scope: Suriname batch 6 — 2028+ oil revenue management architecture: Savings and Stabilization Fund Suriname (SSFS), PFM/fiscal rules, PSC fiscal terms, and the institutional gap still to be closed before first oil.

candidates.title: Savings and Stabilization Fund Suriname (SSFS)
candidates.publisher: Government of Suriname / Ministry of Finance
candidates.description: Sovereign savings and stabilization fund revamped by the 2024 SSFS Act. From 2026, all mineral revenues are to be deposited directly into the fund; annual budgets set a maximum withdrawal consistent with fiscal rules.
candidates.notes: Central institutional node for the oil era. Designed to delink spending from volatile mineral revenues, accumulate assets, and finance the budget only within pre-set limits. Operationalization (investment policy, independent management, transparent reporting) is still incomplete as of mid-2026.

candidates.title: Public Financial Management Law 2024 — fiscal rules
candidates.description: 2024 PFM (Comptabiliteitswet) legislation that embeds two binding fiscal rules: (i) a five-year target for public debt net of SSFS assets, and (ii) annual primary-expenditure ceilings consistent with that debt target.
referenced_by: IMF and rating-agency assessments of fiscal credibility
candidates.notes: Legal backbone of the post-crisis, pre-oil fiscal framework. Intended to prevent a premature spending surge when offshore revenues arrive and to force multi-year planning.

candidates.title: Offshore PSC fiscal terms (royalty, profit oil, tax)
candidates.description: Production-sharing contract fiscal package: 6.25% royalty on gross production, profit-oil split, and 36% corporate income tax. Combined government take estimated in the 60–70% range (after costs) depending on price.
candidates.notes: Contractual revenue-definition node. Continuously cited as the legal basis for the flow of royalty, profit oil and tax that will feed the SSFS once production begins.

candidates.title: Medium-term fiscal framework (MTFF) / multi-year fiscal plan
candidates.description: Requirement under the 2024 PFM law for a multi-year fiscal plan with annual primary-spending ceilings and a clear net-debt target, to be submitted with the budget (starting with 2026/2027).
candidates.notes: Operational planning node. IMF assessments repeatedly stress that agreeing and publishing the five-year plan and expenditure limits is essential to make the fiscal rules credible before oil arrives.

candidates.title: SSFS operationalization gap
candidates.description: Recognised implementation gap: the 2024 SSFS Act exists, but investment policy, independent management, transparent reporting and full deposit of mineral revenues are not yet fully operational.
referenced_by: IMF Article IV and post-financing assessments
candidates.notes: Critical risk node. Continuously cited as the main institutional unfinished business between legislation and the 2028 first-oil date. Without operationalization, the formal rules risk remaining paper constraints.

candidates.title: Net public debt target (debt minus SSFS assets)
candidates.description: Five-year target for public debt net of assets held in the SSFS. Intended anchor of the fiscal rules; IMF staff calibrations have discussed paths toward substantially lower net debt by the early 2030s.
candidates.notes: Sustainability anchor. By measuring debt net of SSFS assets, the framework treats fund accumulation as an explicit offset to gross liabilities.

candidates.title: Definition of mineral / natural-resource revenues for SSFS
candidates.description: Legal and operational definition of which revenues (royalties, profit oil, taxes, dividends, gold, onshore oil, future offshore) must flow into the SSFS. The 2024 Act requires deposit of mineral revenues but leaves some definitional detail to secondary rules.
candidates.notes: Boundary node. Continuously cited as a point that still needs clarifying secondary regulation so that the ‘all mineral revenues into the fund’ rule is unambiguous once offshore flows begin.

candidates.title: Intergenerational equity objective
candidates.publisher: SSFS Act / Green Paper on Fiscal Rules / IMF
candidates.description: Stated policy objective that a portion of oil wealth should be saved for future generations and for precautionary buffers, rather than fully consumed in the boom years.
referenced_by: Public debate on the oil windfall
candidates.notes: Normative design principle. Continuously cited as the rationale for the savings component of the SSFS alongside the pure stabilisation function.

proposed_edges.basis: The SSFS is the operational instrument through which the fiscal rules are implemented (deposit of mineral revenues, limited withdrawals).
The multi-year fiscal plan is the vehicle that sets the debt target and expenditure ceilings required by the PFM law.
PSC terms define the royalty, profit-oil and tax flows that will arise from GranMorgu production.
Mineral revenues are the inflows that the SSFS is designed to receive.
Operationalization is the implementation status of the SSFS legal framework.
The net-debt target is one of the two explicit fiscal rules.
Clear definition of mineral revenues is required for the deposit rule to function.
Intergenerational equity is a stated purpose of the savings component of the fund.
